title: Stagemanager oncall quickmap
content:
Purpose:
Quick field guide for the "stage manager" on-call shift. This is intentionally compact — the goal is enough context + commands to triage and stabilize fast, then handover notes for the next shift.

Shift summary (what I leave behind):
- Current phase: Canary rollout for runtime 2.1.3 to us-west-2. Canary at 10% traffic.
- Known flaky: short-lived OOMs in model-server pod when sequence-length > 4096 (happened twice last 8h).
- Active alerts: latency_p50 > 150ms (warn), model-server OOMKilled (critical, 2 events), autoscaler unstable (flapping).
- Recent actions: rolled back a canary sidecar change 03:20 PST to restore KV cache TTL; restarted autoscaler controller.

Triage checklist (first 10 mins):
1) Check Gaia dashboard overview (Console -> Per-route latency) for spikes and affected routes.
2) Prometheus quick queries (kubectl port-forward to prometheus if needed)
   - p50: sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (route) -> quick compare
   - OOM count: increase(rate(kube_pod_container_status_terminated_reason{reason="OOMKilled"}[15m]))
3) Pods status:
   - kubectl -n inference get pods -o wide -l app=model-server
   - kubectl -n inference describe pod <pod> (if OOMKilled) -> look for memory request/limit and recent Eviction messages
4) Check logs (for suspect pod):
   - kubectl -n inference logs <pod> -c model-server --tail=200 | sed -n '1,200p'
   - journalctl -u redwood-runtime -f (on host, when investigating host-level OOMs)

Fast mitigations (use smallest blast radius):
- If OOMs continue: patch deployment to lower max-seq default OR set default request/limit to safe values: patch-with-cm 'runtime.defaults.max_seq=2048' (temporary) and redeploy canary only.
- If autoscaler flaps: scale replicas manually to stable midpoint: kubectl -n inference scale deployment/model-server --replicas=6. Monitor CPU/Memory for 10m.
- If latency spike isolated to one region: route traffic to fallback region via Smart routing -> set policy "route-fallback: us-east-1" for affected customer segments.

Rollback rules (when to roll back canary):
- Rollback immediately if: repeatable OOM, p95 > 500ms for 15+ minutes on primary routes, or error-rate bump > 3x baseline.
- Use: github.com/redwood/inference/actions -> revert PR (PR:1987) -> deploy previous image tag: redwood/runtime:2.1.2-canary -> run smoke tests.

Escalation matrix (fast):
- 1st: on-call (you) -> post alert summary to #platform-oncall + tag SRE lead (Diego Navarro).
- 2nd: if >30m without stable mitigation -> call SRE lead desk (Diego) and PM on call (Marta).
- Pager escalation: follow standard rotation in PagerDuty (link in #platform-oncall pinned).

Handover notes (what to write for next shift):
- Time window of instability (UTC): 2026-02-12 07:10 -> 08:05
- Actions tried: manual scale to 6 replicas, patched runtime.defaults.max_seq to 2048 on canary, restarted autoscaler, rolled back deployment sidecar change earlier this morning.
- Observed outcome: after scale + patch latency p95 dropped ~35% in 12m, no new OOMs in 40m. Canary traffic resumed at 5% and holding.

Short snippets I use (copy/paste):
- Describe pod with recent term: kubectl -n inference get pod -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.status.containerStatuses[].lastState.terminated != null) | .metadata.name' | xargs -n1 -I{} kubectl -n inference describe pod {}
- Tail logs across nodes (helpful for correlated spikes): kubectl -n inference logs -l app=model-server -c model-server --since=30m --tail=500 | sed -n '1,500p'
- Quick CPU/Memory per pod: kubectl top pods -n inference --containers | grep model-server

Known workarounds (temp):
- If model-server fails to cold-start due to heavy KV load: restart sidecars on 1/3 of pods sequentially: kubectl -n inference rollout restart deployment/model-server --max-unavailable=1 --min-ready-seconds=30
- If cache TTL bug reappears: disable KV TTL enforcement by flipping feature flag in configmaps: cm runtime-flags -> set cache.enforce_ttl=false (remember to revert and log change)

Open/questions / TODOs for follow-up:
- Confirm if OOMs were from single large request pattern (long sequences) or memory leak: run heap profile on suspected pod (SRE/RTE pairing needed).
- Add a smoke test to canary pipeline that emulates high sequence-length prompts (follow-up ticket RED-1909).
- Consider raising memory limits for model-server in 2.1.x until quantization + mem fixes land.

Notes to self (personal reminders):
- When paging the PM, include: affected routes, % traffic impacted, mitigation done, next steps. One-line TL;DR at top of slack post.
- Keep operations changes minimal on my watch. Prefer scaling + routing over config flips unless confident.

Handover checklist (5 lines to paste into next-shift message):
- Status: Stabilized (latency down, no new OOMs in last 40m).
- Actions: scaled model-server ->6, patched max_seq->2048 on canary, restarted autoscaler controller.
- Next steps: observe next 3 deploy windows, run heap profile if OOMs return, create RED-1909 smoke test.
- Contacts: Diego Navarro (SRE lead), Marta O'Connell (PM oncall).
- Links: RED-1842 (incident), PR#1987 (canary), pinned slack thread.

End of quickmap. Keep this doc short and update if the situation changes.

-- Aisha
